headline: 2,158 hospitalised in a day: Dengue admissions hit new daily high
summary: Six more people died and a record number of patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh in the last 24 hours, according to the DGHS.

caption:
A record-breaking surge in dengue cases is hitting Bangladesh, with 2,158 people hospitalised in just 24 hours.

Bangladesh has reported six new dengue deaths and a record 2,158 hospital admissions over the last 24 hours, the highest single-day count this year.

The previous record was set last Tuesday, with 1,872 people admitted. The total death toll for the year has reached 225, with 128 of those deaths occurring in September alone.

In the capital, Dhaka North City Corporation recorded 311 admissions, while Dhaka South recorded 197. Another 356 patients were admitted to hospitals in the Dhaka Division outside the city corporations.

Other regions also saw significant numbers: Chattogram recorded 345 admissions, Khulna 329, Barishal 227, Rajshahi 176, Mymensingh 132, Rangpur 73, and Sylhet 12.

So far this year, 73,694 people have been hospitalised with the Aedes mosquito-borne disease, and 68,006 have been discharged.

The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has tracked these statistics since 2000. The disease peaked in 2023, with a record 321,179 admissions and 1,705 deaths in a single year.

headline: TIB and HRSS condemn attacks on health centre and studio
summary: Transparency International Bangladesh and the Human Rights Support Society demand accountability and impartial probes into the vandalism of a Mirpur health centre and Salman Muqtadir's studio.
details: Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) and the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) have condemned attacks on the Radda MCH-FP healthcare centre in Dhaka's Mirpur and content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.
TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman described the looting and vandalism at the health centre as an "embarrassing example" for the government and the ruling party.

TIB alleged that since the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024, some BNP leaders and activists have been involved in widespread extortion, encroachment, and turf wars across the country.
The TIB chief warned that continued allegations of encroachment and extortion involving BNP leaders could erode the public mandate the party received after the July Uprising.
HRSS Executive Director Ijajul Islam stated that these incidents are serious violations of people's rights to life, security, healthcare, and property.
HRSS called for independent investigations into the attacks, including allegations of police negligence or collusion, and demanded the recovery of looted vaccines and medical equipment.
The health centre in Mirpur-1 was reportedly looted and vandalised at midnight, allegedly with the backing of a reserved-seat MP.
TIB also referred to clashes between two factions of the local BNP unit in Kishoreganj over a water body, which left more than 50 people injured.
caption:
TIB and HRSS warn that widespread extortion and encroachment by some political activists could erode public trust in the new government.

Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) and the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) have condemned attacks on the Radda MCH-FP healthcare centre in Dhaka's Mirpur and content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.

TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman described the looting and vandalism at the health centre as an "embarrassing example" for the government and the ruling party.

TIB alleged that since the fall of the Awami League government in August 2024, some BNP leaders and activists have been involved in widespread extortion, encroachment, and turf wars across the country.

The TIB chief warned that continued allegations of encroachment and extortion involving BNP leaders could erode the public mandate the party received after the July Uprising.

HRSS Executive Director Ijajul Islam stated that these incidents are serious violations of people's rights to life, security, healthcare, and property.

HRSS called for independent investigations into the attacks, including allegations of police negligence or collusion, and demanded the recovery of looted vaccines and medical equipment.

The health centre in Mirpur-1 was reportedly looted and vandalised at midnight, allegedly with the backing of a reserved-seat MP.

TIB also referred to clashes between two factions of the local BNP unit in Kishoreganj over a water body, which left more than 50 people injured.
